source_name: Jooble Hungary (hu.jooble.org) — meta-aggregator of HU job ads
why_relevant: Meta-aggregator that indexes small/regional boards and employer sites that profession.hu and Indeed miss; useful as a completeness net and as a fetchable mirror when primary ATS pages are bot-defended. Employer-keyed URLs (állás-kpmg, állás-pwc, állás-deloitte) are stable.

source_name: CVOnline.hu — #2 Hungarian job board
why_relevant: Second-largest HU board by market share (per HR Portal / Dolgozom.hu rankings); carries bank and financial-services ads not always cross-posted to profession.hu, widening coverage of mid-tier institutions and vendors.

source_name: Jobline.hu — HVG's job portal (since 2000)
why_relevant: Third-largest HU board, media-affiliated (HVG); white-collar and graduate financial-sector ads. Complementary coverage plus editorial career content that occasionally names hiring waves in banking.

source_name: HR Portal — 'Állásoldalak' / 'A legjobb álláskereső oldalak' (pointer to the HU job-board landscape)
why_relevant: Maintained, dated inventory of Hungarian job portals with market-share commentary (profession.hu ~90%, CVOnline #2, Jobline #3, Dreamjobs, Jófogás, Zyntern). This is the map that keeps the board list current as portals appear/disappear — plus HR Portal itself reports on sector hiring and organisational change.

source_name: Felvi.hu — 'Állásportálok' directory (higher-education careers service)
why_relevant: Public-sector-maintained directory of Hungarian job portals and career resources; a second, independent pointer inventory to validate the board list and surface graduate/entry channels through which banks staff junior compliance and reporting roles.

source_name: Hays Hungary — specialist banking & finance recruitment
why_relevant: Specialist agency with declared Accountancy & Finance and Banking practices in Budapest. Agency-posted ads often describe a client's regulatory programme anonymously but in detail ('leading bank, DORA implementation'), and agency salary/market reports quantify demand shifts for compliance skills.

source_name: Randstad Hungary — finance/business-support staffing
why_relevant: Large staffing provider covering finance, accounting and business support in HU, including contract/interim staffing that banks use for time-boxed regulatory programmes — interim hiring spikes are an unusually sharp deadline signal.

source_name: JobsGarden — HU recruitment agency (finance, IT, business administration)
why_relevant: 15+ years placing finance and IT staff in Hungary; mid-market agency whose ads reach institutions too small to run visible career portals (savings/credit institutions, PSPs, vendors) — the tail of the regulatory-hiring signal.

source_name: Allasod.hu — HU job aggregator with employer-keyed pages (e.g. Magyar Nemzeti Bank)
why_relevant: Employer-keyed aggregator URLs give a lightweight, fetchable watchlist per institution (observed with an MNB page listing new vacancies), useful as a redundant channel when the primary career portal is JS-heavy or defended.

source_name: MNB – Szakmai konzultációk (Supervisory professional consultations, agendas + downloadable presentations)
why_relevant: The central bank/supervisor's own recurring practitioner consultation series; each event page carries the agenda, the MNB directorate/speaker names and the slide decks, which is the earliest signal of which recommendations, decrees and reporting obligations MNB intends to enforce next.

source_name: MNB – Pénzforgalmi konzultáció oldal (payments consultation hub)
why_relevant: Dedicated payments-consultation entry point; consultations on MNB decrees on payment execution are announced here with comment deadlines, and consultation rounds are typically paired with industry workshops.

source_name: MNB – Konferenciák, előadások (Financial Stability conference & presentation archive)
why_relevant: Archive of MNB conference appearances and presentation decks in the financial-stability/supervision area — decks by named MNB executives often pre-announce regulatory intentions before formal publication.

source_name: MNB – Lámfalussy Lectures Konferencia
why_relevant: MNB's flagship annual conference; programme and speaker roster identify which international and domestic policy themes the central bank is elevating, and reports of past editions are published with the agenda.

source_name: MNB Zöld Pénzügyek – események (green finance events)
why_relevant: Event calendar for MNB's green-finance workstream, where ESG-related supervisory expectations for banks are trailed ahead of formal recommendations.

source_name: Portfolio.hu Rendezvények – conference portfolio (Financial IT, Future of Finance, Hitelezés, Bankjövő)
why_relevant: The dominant commercial organiser of Hungarian banking/payments conferences; per-event Program and Előadók pages give session-level agendas plus named MNB, ministry and bank speakers — a high-density forecast of imminent obligations (AFR, ISO 20022, DORA, PSD3/PSR).

source_name: Nemzetközi Bankárképző Központ (International Training Center for Bankers) – programmes & conferences
why_relevant: The banking sector's main training institution; individual course pages are explicitly tied to specific MNB decrees and recommendations (e.g. MiFID II training per MNB Decree 37/2017, payment-fraud course per MNB Recommendation 5/2023), so the course catalogue is a near-real-time index of which compliance obligations banks are actually staffing up for.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Hírek, aktualitások
why_relevant: The banking association's news stream announces its own professional events, working-group activity and joint events with Bankárképző; the association is the collective counterparty in MNB consultations, so its event topics reveal the industry-side regulatory agenda.

source_name: FinTechZone – PayTechShow / TechShow X event programme
why_relevant: Hungarian payments-industry show whose published programme lists sessions explicitly on PSD3/PSR, payment licensing changes and the NIS2/DORA/AI Act stack, with MNB representatives among speakers — a compact map of who owns each regulatory workstream.

source_name: paytech.events – TechShow X Budapest 2026 listing and 2026–2027 fintech/payments conference calendar
why_relevant: English-language aggregator that describes the Hungarian event's agenda themes (instant payments/AFR evolution, ISO 20022, EU Instant Payments Regulation, DORA) and attendee mix including MNB regulators; useful as a discovery index for events not indexed in Hungarian sources.

source_name: Digital Payment konferencia (digitalpayment.hu) – programme and speakers
why_relevant: Recurring Hungarian payments conference whose programme names MNB Financial Infrastructure & Payment Systems Directorate analysts as speakers and focuses on AFR/qvik evolution — direct evidence of which payment-infrastructure obligations are next.

source_name: Financial Fraud Summit / Pénzforgalom és kiberbiztonság konferencia (ffs.ap.hu)
why_relevant: Dedicated payments-fraud and cyber event covering PSD3/PSR expectations, KVR (central fraud-data system), qvik and AI-based fraud defence, with regulators and bank leaders on the agenda — a focused view of supervisory expectations on fraud reporting.

source_name: IVSZ – Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége, események
why_relevant: ICT trade association whose event listing carries and co-brands financial-sector regulatory events (e.g. Financial Fraud Summit) and NIS2/DORA-adjacent programmes; a good secondary discovery feed.

source_name: IIR Hungary – banking/payments training and conference calendar
why_relevant: Long-running commercial conference/training organiser for the Hungarian financial sector (card market, digital payments, compliance); its paid-seminar catalogue is a demand signal for which regulatory topics banks will pay to be trained on.

source_name: Budapest Institute of Banking (BIB) – banking education and MNB educational cooperation
why_relevant: MNB-linked banking education body; its course and event programme shows which supervisory themes the central bank wants embedded in practitioner training, an early proxy for enforcement priorities.

source_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség (Hungarian Fintech Association) – hunfintech.com
why_relevant: 67-member association with education as an explicit pillar; co-organiser of Budapest Fintech Week and partner of regional events, and the industry voice in payment-licensing/PSD3 debates — its event and position output names the practitioners driving each file.

source_name: Big-4 Hungary regulatory webinar series (PwC Magyarország FS webinars; KPMG Hungary insights/events; EY Hungary DORA)
why_relevant: Advisory-firm webinars and their landing pages are a reliable leading indicator of near-term compliance deadlines (PSD2 review→PSD3/PSR, DORA application date, MNB AI expectations); registration pages carry the agenda and named partner speakers.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. (payment infrastructure operator) – company/professional day materials
why_relevant: Operator of the Hungarian clearing infrastructure (BKR/AFR); its professional days and client-facing communications set the technical migration deadlines (ISO 20022, AFR releases) that banks must meet, complementing MNB's regulatory calendar.
